clue.text: They might circle several core planets, after one take-off

indicators.note: to circle the letters is to send them round into a new order
take-off asks for the letters of the word one to be removed from the pool before rearranging

parts.note: the word one, whose letters are stripped from the pool

explanation.surface: A thought about spacecraft orbiting a group of central planets once they have launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might circle' and 'after one take-off' work together: drop O, N, E from SEVERALCOREPLANETS and rearrange the remaining fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts and other voyagers beyond Earth are the people referred to by the pronoun, and they might well orbit planets.

clue.text: Location of new tiny arrivals, initially

definitions.text: Location of new tiny arrivals, initially

parts.note: a location is a place

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A question about where newborn babies are to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the organ in the womb that nourishes developing babies, so it doubles as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ attached to the womb wall is literally where an unborn baby develops before arrival.

clue.text: Tin found following small survey

indicators.note: following places the tin's letters after the abbreviation for small

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A tin can turns up after a modest inspection of the area.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey something is to look it over carefully, a close synonym of examining or scrutinising it.

clue.text: Mature as pickled hams

indicators.note: pickled means preserved or drunk, so the letters are muddled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Hams maturing as they are cured in brine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hams' looks like meat to go with 'pickled', but it means poor actors; Mature plus as is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hams are inexpert performers, and non-professional performers are a close equivalent in this crossword sense.

clue.text: Old 10's above short man's temper

indicators.note: above, in a down clue, puts the queen's name on top of the short name

parts.note: 10 across is QUEEN, and Anne is an old queen of England
Al is a short form of a man's name such as Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A former monarch sits higher than a little man's angry mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' as a noun suggests anger, but here it is the verb used of toughening metal or glass by heating.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper metal or glass is to heat and slowly cool it, the same metallurgical process.

clue.text: Mark nicks one in four with one on patrol

indicators.note: nicks here means takes in or steals, so the mark holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a quad is one of quadruplets, so one baby in a set of four

explanation.surface: A mark cuts into one of four people alongside a guard on the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters for the quadruplet go after the first letter of the mark, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A police vehicle on patrol is a car that does rounds, here personified as one on patrol.

clue.text: Solution bottled in litres, ultimately

indicators.note: bottled in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A liquid answer that comes in bottles measured by the litre in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or answer to a problem, as in the outcome of a sum, is its solution.

clue.text: Brown's work for England made sons rebel

indicators.note: to rebel is to rise up against order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tale of English sons turning against their country.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is Dan Brown, the American thriller writer; the novel is his follow-up-of-sorts to The Da Vinci Code.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a Dan Brown thriller, so it is a work by that author.

clue.text: Copper pot endlessly cooked nice meal, lacking energy

indicators.note: endlessly asks for the last letter of the word pot to be cut off
cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are mixed up
lacking asks for the letter for energy to be dropped from the meal before mixing

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cook makes a pleasant dinner from a pot but it lacks vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a metal pot to match the kitchen, but it is slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is British slang for a police officer, one who cops or catches criminals.

clue.text: Mercury's group on board?

definitions.meaning: Freddie Mercury was the singer of the rock band of this name
on a chessboard this is the most powerful piece

explanation.definitionFit: Freddie Mercury fronted the rock band of this name, and the chess piece stands on the board.

clue.text: Chanel's biggest fan might be shy

parts.note: Coco was the first name of the designer Gabrielle Chanel
a nut is an enthusiast, a devoted fan

explanation.surface: The keenest admirer of the fashion house might be bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where people throw balls to knock coconuts off posts, so the fruit 'might be' followed by shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground game is called a coconut shy, so this tropical fruit can precede the word shy.

clue.text: '80s band dates '80s musician

parts.note: eras are periods of time, dates in history
Midge Ure was a Scottish musician famous in the 1980s with Ultravox

explanation.surface: A 1980s pop group goes out with a pop star of the same decade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dates' suggests romance between two acts, but it means periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a British synth-pop duo of Vince Clarke and Andy Bell that had hits throughout the 1980s.

clue.text: Bronze knight, fighting machine

parts.note: a tan is a bronze colour on the skin
K is the chess notation for king, but N or K stands for knight in crosswords; here K

explanation.surface: A suntanned knight on horseback ready for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured tracked military vehicle is the classic battlefield fighting machine.

clue.text: Carbon copies are plastic, due to manufacture

indicators.note: to manufacture is to make up, so the letters are fashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: Copies are made of plastic because of how they are produced.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon copies are exact replicas of an original document, the same as replicas or doubles.

clue.text: Argonaut thrown into faraway land

indicators.note: into puts the thrown piece inside the faraway country's abbreviation

parts.note: AUS is short for Australia, seen from Britain as a land far away
cast means thrown, as a line or a stone

explanation.surface: A sailor of the Argo is hurled into a distant country.
explanation.definitionFit: Acastus was one of the heroes in Greek myth who sailed with Jason on the Argo.

clue.text: Love to run around island with energy? Not me!

definitions.text: Love to run around island with energy? Not me!

indicators.note: around turns the zero and the jogging word round together so they read backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
to trot is to run at a gentle pace
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they fancy a vigorous jog round the island, and declines.
explanation.walkthrough: The slow reptile famously beat the hare, but would never volunteer to run energetically, so the whole clue is its reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow shelled reptile is the creature least likely to want to run anywhere with vigour.

clue.text: Platinum blonde plays any minor role after film's finale

indicators.note: after puts the reworked letters behind the film's closing letter
finale asks for the closing letter of the word film's
plays suggests performing in various ways, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peroxide star takes a bit part once a movie has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ANY MINOR ROLE gives ARILYN MONROE, following M.
explanation.definitionFit: The film star was famous for her platinum-blonde hair, making her the archetypal platinum blonde.

clue.text: Iron, it was forged in my childhood

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the word my
was forged means made or faked, so the letters are hammered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remembers iron being worked by a smith when they were young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like a metal being forged in a smithy, but only its four letters are shaken up, with it kept as written; 'in' places the lot within my.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under the legal age of adulthood is the state of being a minor, i.e. childhood.

clue.text: A nautical way to pull fish up by pole

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, reads the pulling word and the fish from bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to pull, as a cart
an eel is a fish
S stands for South, one of the earth's poles

explanation.surface: Instructions for landing a catch by hauling it up with a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use the term for the direction downwind, away from where the wind is coming.

clue.text: Buff over me in sparkle test

indicators.note: over means covering, so the buff wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast and expert

indicators.note: sparkle suggests fizzing about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An enthusiast covers someone in glitter as some kind of trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkle' reads like glitter in the surface but signals that the two short words me and in are jumbled; 'Buff' means an enthusiast, not polish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial carried out to find out what happens is a scientific test.

clue.text: Silver — perhaps small change's rising cost?

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, reads the coin's letters upwards

parts.note: 1p, one penny, is small change, written with I for 1
rate is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: Asks whether the cost of silver keeps going up with loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' looks like the metal or cash, but it is Long John Silver of Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the buccaneer in Stevenson's Treasure Island, an example of a seafaring robber.

clue.text: See 17 across
Lead man of our time

parts.note: he refers to a man
AD, Anno Domini, labels years of the present era

explanation.surface: The leading man of the present generation.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead something is to be in charge of it, which is what heading it means.

clue.text: Fool swallows 'ard piece of bacon

indicators.note: swallows means takes in, so the fool encloses the other letters

parts.note: a loon is a fool
'ard is hard with the H dropped, giving the letters as printed after the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An idiot gulps down a tough piece of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of fat bacon threaded through lean meat in cooking is this, a variant of lardon.

clue.text: Take back miracle cure

indicators.note: cure suggests treating or processing, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Recovering a lost item through a wonder remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something that was yours, or retract it, is to take it back.

clue.text: Nickel possibly two thirds of Alnico compound

indicators.note: compound means mixed, so the remaining letters are combined anew
two thirds of the six-letter word Alnico leaves its last four letters

explanation.surface: An alloy of aluminium, nickel and cobalt explained as a mix.
explanation.walkthrough: Alnico is a magnetic alloy; two thirds of it is NICO, which rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American five-cent piece, an example of a piece of money.

clue.text: Services and repairs audio

indicators.note: audio says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rights means puts right or repairs

explanation.surface: Maintenance and fixing for sound equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious ceremonies such as funerals and weddings are church services.

clue.text: Journeyed beyond, round Uranus first, then Earth — spinning and hollow

parts.note: a round shape is like the letter O

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of Uranus
spinning turns the soil word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: earth is dirt, soil
a den is a hollow or lair

explanation.surface: A spacecraft passes the planets, circling Uranus, then a rotating, empty Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ridden further than someone or past a point is to have journeyed beyond it.
